pr_title: C#: Avoid GodotSharp as project assembly name
pr_body:
- The name GodotSharp conflicts with the name of the Godot assembly, this causes a cyclic dependency.
- Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/63041.
pr_comments:
Same thing will (probably) happen for `GodotSharpEditor`, `Godot.SourceGenerators`, and the name of any other package (indirectly) referenced by the project.

I would say if we do this we should at least add the other godot packages to this check as well.
That's true, I was thinking it'd be nice to refactor this logic so it's in a single place and then I remembered that you have a similar PR (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/74516).

issue_context.title: Naming a project GodotSharp causes c# scripts not to work.
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v3.4.4.stable.mono.official [419e713a2]

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Trying out the c# functionality of Godot I created a project called GodotSharp.
I added a node with a simple c# script.

Upon pressing play in the editor i get the following error in the CMD window and the Debugger>Errors view:
`
E 0:00:02.359   can_instance: Cannot instance script because the class 'TestNode' could not be found. Script: 'res://TestNode.cs'.
  <C++ Error>   Method failed. Returning: __null
  <C++ Source>  modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2892 @ can_instance()
`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new project with the name GodotSharp. 
2. Create a root node and attach a C# script to it.
3. Press Play in the editor.
4. See the error in the console.

Discord user 'the31' figured out that this is due to a clash with a built in DLL.
Changing the project name fixes the issue. 

It would be helpful with better error messaging or even declining to create a project with this name.

### Minimal reproduction project
[GodotSharp.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9122316/GodotSharp.zip)

review_comments: Is there a specific reason not to respect the feature overrides here? Or asked otherwise, why did we take them into account originally?
